title: Transfer program: from the ISLA audit to testable mechanisms
text:
What this program tests
Thesis. The audit of the ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention) research record (the companion review in research/cross_dataset_generalization/, an untracked directory whose rendered report is _book/index.html there) concluded that the record does not establish a cross-dataset accuracy advantage, and that the promising targets are a complete physical input, a stable computational representation, and reusable components of the physical response. This program turns that agenda into experiments with preregistered bars, in the order the audit recommended: first the controls that make any later result interpretable (paired physical conditions, source-only normalization, and a pressure-offset versus spatial-error decomposition), then, in parallel, the computational-support study on the existing DrivAerML volume task and the nonlearned gates for the three response-based directions (boundary-response rank and basis transfer, local-response composition, solver correction spaces). A separate chapter asks what classical solvers do that learned surrogates do not, as a source of further hypotheses.
Utility. The quantity that matters is field and force error on geometries and dataset families outside the training distribution, with the PDE, boundary conditions, dimensionless parameters and label convention stated; with query and mesh consistency; and with the total cost counted (preprocessing, target-operator access, iterations, adaptation labels). A result that improves a fixed-mesh in-family score without moving that quantity is not progress here.
How to read this. Every chapter states current knowledge and the preregistered bar that would change it; the dated record of what was tried, in what order, is the notebook. Numbers in chapters are computed from checked-in artifacts under studies/. Verdicts follow bars written before the readout; amendments to an instrument are recorded before its numbers are read. Architectures are named (ISLA, GeoTransolver, Transolver); ratios are baseline error divided by ISLA error unless a chapter says otherwise.

title: 1  Controls before experiments
text:
1.1 C1: offset or spatial error
The DrivAerML → SHIFT-SUV zero-shot failure is a spatial field error, not a pressure-reference offset; the transfer configurations’ normalizations are source-only in effect for the reported metrics; and the paired physical-condition control is being measured on an exactly specified problem. These three controls were the audit’s prerequisites for any architectural experiment on transfer, because each names a way a transfer comparison can be wrong before it says anything about a model.
A model that predicts a sensible field about the wrong constant has a relative L2 error near 1.0, which is where ISLA’s source-only fastback error sat (0.99 against GeoTransolver’s 0.59, three seeds each). DrivAerML and SHIFT-SUV are simulated with different ground and wheel conditions, freestream speeds and solvers, and pressure is nondimensionalized by each case’s dynamic pressure with no shift, so a reference difference between the datasets would appear as a per-case constant. The diagnostic decomposes each arm’s error, from the saved zero-shot predictions, into the area-weighted mean (the offset) and the centered remainder, and checks whether the offset cancels from the integrated pressure force, as it must on a closed surface with consistent normals (Section 2 for the preregistered bars).
The constant carries 1.5% (ISLA) and 3.0% (GeoTransolver) of the source-only squared error by the median over cases, against a 20% floor for the “spatial” band; removing it changes the relative error by under 1%, and the in-family arms pass the instrument check with offset shares under 1%. The offsets that do exist are small and of the same sign for both models (+0.14 of the true field’s RMS), consistent with a modest reference difference that explains none of the gap. The failure is a field error, and it is a force error: 1.6x (ISLA) and 1.4x (GeoTransolver) of the true force magnitude against 0.04 in-family, falling to 0.28 and 0.20 when the estate family joins training. Two consequences: the pressure-reference hypothesis is closed, and every transfer claim in this program reports the force error beside the field error, since a field error of 0.9 is a force error above 100%. What remains as the leading non-architectural explanation is the compound physical-condition mismatch between the datasets, which C3 tests in its exact form.

title: 1  Controls before experiments
text:
1.2 C2: source-only normalization
Both transfer configurations nondimensionalize pressure and wall shear by each case’s own dynamic pressure with no shift, and normalize wall shear by a declared per-dataset constant (standard deviation 0.00313 for DrivAerML, 0.00183 for SHIFT-SUV, zero mean). Inference denormalizes predictions with the statistics saved at training time, which are the source’s, and the relative L2 metric is invariant to a common scale, so the differing wall-shear constants do not bias the reported relative errors; they would bias an absolute or mixed-field loss, and a zero-shot protocol should carry the source’s constant into the target configuration. Pressure carries no constant beyond the physical nondimensionalization, so C1 is not a normalization artifact. Verdict: source-only in effect for the reported metrics, with one declared-constant hygiene rule (Section 5).

title: 1  Controls before experiments
section: 1.3 C3: a paired physical condition on an exact problem
text:
1.3 C3: a paired physical condition on an exact problem
The audit’s identifiability argument says that a model which does not see a physical condition faces an irreducible floor when that condition varies across cases with identical geometry, and that the floor is a property of the information, not the architecture. C3 measures this on exterior potential flow: the same bodies in free air and at a fixed height above a ground plane (an image-method reference qualified against the sphere’s analytic pressure), with a small ISLA trained with and without the ground condition as an input, three seeds, held-out shapes. Bars and the equal-mixture floor are preregistered in the study’s own file (studies/paired_conditions/PREREG.md); the result is not yet measured (Section 1 lists the schedule). What it licenses, if it behaves as predicted, is a statement about the DrivAerML → SHIFT-SUV shift: the ground and wheel motion, the speed and the solver are conditions the current encoding does not see, and their effect on the field is bounded below by a floor no architecture can cross without the information; what it does not license is any estimate of how large that floor is on the real datasets, which needs paired simulations that do not exist.

title: 4  Local-response composition
text:
4.1 The gate
Composing exact local port responses into new assemblies is exact, but errors in the smooth part of a local response are amplified 4–30x by the interface solve and grow superlinearly with assembly size on grids, while errors in the rough part are damped 20–100x; port reduction that transfers to new shapes compresses nothing at the 1% level. The audit’s third direction proposed learning local Dirichlet-to-Neumann responses in compatible port coordinates and enforcing global compatibility numerically, so that a new arrangement of familiar parts is not a new shape. The nonlearned gate asked how interface-solve error propagates when local responses are inexact, before any predictor is trained. The answer rejects the direction as proposed and points at a narrower hybrid.
Linear finite elements on unit-square components with identical straight ports (64 perimeter nodes, 15 interior nodes per shared edge), a library of five shapes (plain, coefficient contrast, hole, wide and narrow internal channels) and three held-out shapes (offset hole, diagonal barrier, an eight-cell checkerboard); assemblies in chains and grids of 2, 4, 8 and 16 components, five random draws each, against a monolithic finite-element reference; a screened variant as control. The exact machinery passes every check: response symmetry, positive semidefiniteness, the constant null vector, the Schur-complement composition law against a merged-mesh Schur complement (2 × 10⁻¹⁶), and an exact interface solve (5 × 10⁻¹⁵ energy error). Every component response is then perturbed by a relative Frobenius error ε (random, or concentrated on smooth or on rough port modes), and reduced responses are built by transfer-optimal port modes and by equal-rank proper orthogonal decomposition. Bars, written before the run (studies/composition/PREREG.md): worth a learner if the global energy error stays below 5% at ε = 10⁻² from 2 to 8 components with no faster than square-root growth, and if transfer-optimal reduction reaches 1% at a quarter of the port dimension on new assemblies of new shapes; not worth it if local errors amplify superlinearly or the interface solve costs more than the monolithic one.

At ε = 10⁻² the 5% bar is missed for chains of 8 or more and for every grid; from 4 to 16 components the grid error grows 6.2x, faster than linear. The mechanism is in the last two columns: errors on rough port modes are attenuated 20–100x by the interface solve, errors on smooth modes are amplified 4–30x and set the global error, because the smooth, small-eigenvalue part of a response is the load-bearing part (truncating the response itself to fewer than 63 of 64 modes gives errors of 10² to 10⁷). Port reduction confirms it from the other side: transfer-optimal modes built from a plain reference pair do transfer to new shapes, but need 13–15 of 15 modes for 1%, while proper-orthogonal modes need all 15 on new shapes (they are shape-specific); at rank 4 both leave 16–27% error. The interface solve is cheaper than the monolithic one only up to four components, and the partition-of-unity coarse space does not reduce the interface iteration count. The narrow-channel family did not exercise a near-port singularity (the barrier sits inside the component), which is a limitation of this instrument, not a finding.

title: 4  Local-response composition
text:
4.3 What this changes
As proposed, a learned local response would need a relative error near 10⁻³ on smooth port modes to reach 2% on a 4 × 4 assembly, at full port rank, with reciprocity, positive semidefiniteness and the null vector preserved exactly; that is a stricter target than any learned response in the literature reaches, and the direction stops in that form. What survives is a hybrid: keep the smooth low-mode response exact (a coarse local solve or an analytic expansion) and learn only the rough remainder, whose errors the interface solve damps. That is a solver with a learned component, not a field regressor, and it is the same shape as the audit’s exterior variant (analytic multipole coupling, learned near-field maps) and as the wall-law and constraint-solve hypotheses of Chapter 6. Its next nonlearned test is a split response (exact low modes plus a perturbed remainder) and a barrier-adjacent-to-port family for the near-field claim; neither is launched here. The instrument is 2D scalar diffusion with shared straight ports; convection removes the energy-norm certificate, elasticity adds rigid modes per component, and exterior aerodynamics has no shared ports at all.

title: 5  Transferring a solver correction space
text:
5.1 The probe
A frozen correction space fitted on source geometries transfers worse than a free geometric coarse grid on every held-out discrete elliptic system tested, so the direction stops for that class. The audit’s fourth direction proposed learning a coarse correction space or preconditioner on source problems and letting the correct target operator finish the solve, the reasoning being that slow error modes might transfer more reliably than whole fields. The nonlearned probe asked whether any frozen source-derived space beats an equally cheap classical one; if not, a network trained to produce such a space would start behind a construction that costs nothing to learn. It does not.
Linear finite elements on the unit square with circular Neumann holes and a piecewise-constant coefficient inclusion; Dirichlet data lifted and eliminated so the diffusion operator is symmetric positive definite (about 2,000–2,200 unknowns). Twenty source geometries; three held-out sets of eight each: new hole positions within the family, a topology shift (two holes, or a hole two to three cells from the wall), and a tenfold larger coefficient contrast. Correction spaces of dimension 16 and 32: a frozen proper orthogonal decomposition of source errors that survive three damped-Jacobi sweeps (ten smooth right-hand sides per source geometry, registered to a shared background grid), a per-target oracle decomposition of the same kind (an upper bound, not deployable), and three classical spaces of the same dimension (piecewise-constant aggregation, smoothed aggregation, a bilinear geometric coarse grid). Readouts: the energy-norm error left after one Galerkin coarse correction on random, slow (generalized eigenvectors 4–20) and near-null (eigenvectors 1–3) error directions; and complete two-level conjugate-gradient solves to a relative residual of 10⁻⁸ with setup amortized over ten right-hand sides. Bars, written before the run: advance only if the frozen source space halves the slow-mode error left by the best classical space within family and improves it by 1.5x under the topology shift, and saves at least 20% of total work; stop if a classical space matches or beats it on either held-out set (studies/solver_spaces/PREREG.md).

On near-null probes at rank 32 the frozen space leaves 0.53 of the error, the oracle 0.42, the geometric grid 0.37. In complete solves the frozen space needs 141–162 iterations at rank 16 against 82–99 for the best classical space and 84–104 against 61–72 at rank 32; counting setup, it saves between −19% and −72% of the work, so no break-even number of right-hand sides exists. Every solve converged; on the symmetric problem residual and energy-norm error contract together, so the residual-not-error failure the audit warned of does not arise here.
The mechanism is visible in the source spectrum. The smoother-resistant source errors are low-dimensional (normalized singular values 0.10, 0.06, 0.04, 0.02 at modes 2, 5, 9, 17), but their span is that of the smooth right-hand sides used to generate them around twenty particular hole positions, not the target operator’s slow subspace. The geometric grid spans generic smooth functions, which is the slow space of a discrete elliptic operator under a point smoother, for any geometry, without seeing a source problem. Even the oracle decomposition fitted on the target’s own smoothed errors leaves 0.78 of the slow-mode error against the grid’s 0.47. Solution snapshots are the wrong object to fit a correction space from, and a learner trained on them inherits the mismatch.
The convection–diffusion variant was run and is reported as not measured: at mesh Péclet 0.5 the preconditioned GMRES converges in two to three iterations with any space, and the one-step Galerkin correction is not a projection for a nonsymmetric operator (it increases the slow-mode error for the fitted spaces). A Petrov–Galerkin correction and a higher Péclet number would be needed for that case to discriminate.

title: 5  Transferring a solver correction space
text:
5.3 What this changes
The direction stops for discrete elliptic problems on a fixed discretization: a learned correction space must beat the geometric coarse grid, not the absence of one, and the object to learn would have to be operator-aware (near-null vectors of the target operator, which adaptive algebraic multigrid already computes without learning) rather than fitted to source solutions. Two homes remain for a learned solver component, and each needs a prerequisite gate before any training: operators whose classical coarse spaces demonstrably fail (strong anisotropy, indefinite or high-Péclet operators, state-dependent nonlinear Jacobians, where the audit’s nonlinear extension lives), and learned smoothers or prolongation weights on a classical hierarchy, which are a different object from a frozen space. Chapter Chapter 6 takes up the second as part of the question of what classical solvers do that surrogates do not.
crumbs: 5  Transferring a solver correction space

title: 6  What classical solvers do that surrogates do not
text:
6.1 The inventory
Classical PDE and CFD solvers generalize to new geometries and conditions because almost nothing in them is fitted to a geometry: the physics enters as a local operator, the geometry enters as a mesh and a set of boundary conditions, and the global coupling is produced at run time by iteration and by exact algebra. A learned surrogate inverts every one of those choices at once: it fits the global map on a family, encodes geometry implicitly, and produces the answer in one pass. The audit’s four directions are each an attempt to hand one solver ingredient back to mathematics. This chapter lists the ingredients, states what each buys and what it costs, and derives from each a hypothesis that an experiment in this program can reject. Papers cited in the audit’s two literature dossiers are referenced by name; the mechanism claims here are classical numerical analysis, not new results.
Two patterns run through the table. First, classical solvers separate what is local and universal (the operator, the closure, the wall law) from what is global and case-specific (the solution), and produce the second from the first by iteration or exact algebra at run time. Surrogates learn the global object directly, so they must see the family they are asked about. Second, solvers carry an error estimate in the residual, so they can spend more work where a case is harder; surrogates spend a fixed amount everywhere and report no uncertainty. The audit’s mechanisms chapter adds the caution that a small residual is not a small error without a stability bound, so the residual is a control signal, not a certificate.

title: 6  What classical solvers do that surrogates do not
text:
Ingredient of a classical solver
Why it generalizes
What it costs
What the surrogate does instead




Local discrete operator (finite volume / element stencils)
The same few-point relation holds at every cell of every mesh; geometry enters only through cell metrics
A sparse system whose solve is the whole cost
Fits a global input→output map on one family; the operator is implicit and family-specific


Iterative solve with a residual
Convergence is monitored against the equation, so a new geometry is solved to the same tolerance as a familiar one
Tens to thousands of operator applications
One pass; no residual, no stopping criterion, error unknown until compared to a label


Multigrid / coarse spaces
Smooth error is corrected on a coarse representation that exists for any geometry; the slow space is generic smoothness
Hierarchy construction; a few percent of a solve
Fixed latent size chosen by validation error; the interior spectrum is whatever training produced (Chapter 5 shows source-fitted spaces lose to a free coarse grid)


Domain decomposition and static condensation
Local solves plus a small exact interface system; a component’s response is reusable in any assembly with compatible interfaces
Interface solve; coarse space for scalability
Whole-shape regression; a new arrangement of familiar parts is a new shape


Boundary integral methods
The free-space kernel is universal; geometry enters through a dense but well-understood boundary operator
Dense or fast-multipole-accelerated boundary solve; only for linear homogeneous operators
Learns kernel and inverse together, on a family; the repository’s exact-kernel branch transferred across boundary frequencies where a learned decoder did not


Fast multipole and translation operators
Far-field interactions between separated bodies are analytic expansions; only near-field is geometry-specific
Expansion order; near-field corrections for close bodies
Attention over all tokens learns near and far interactions alike from data


Pressure–velocity coupling (projection, SIMPLE)
The pressure solve enforces a global constraint (mass conservation) exactly at every step
A Poisson solve per step
Pressure is predicted pointwise; conservation is not enforced (the interior chapter of the program book reports pressure as a gauge quantity with no constraint)


Wall models and near-wall resolution
The near-wall region is modelled by a local law (log law, wall function) that is the same on every wall
Mesh grading or a modelled first cell
A uniform token budget; the audit’s harmonic-disk spectrum control shows wall flux needs modes the interior does not


Closure models (RANS, hybrid RANS–LES)
Turbulent stresses are local algebraic or transport relations, calibrated once, applied everywhere
Model error; closure-dependent labels
The surrogate must learn the closure’s imprint from labels; the eddy-viscosity gap (1.26x, program book) may be exactly this


Newton / Jacobian-based nonlinear solves
Local linearization gives quadratic convergence near a solution on any geometry
Jacobian assembly or its action; globalization
No state to linearize around; branch and regime are not represented (regime extrapolation fails ~10x for every architecture tested)


Continuation in a parameter
A solution at one condition initializes the next; branches are tracked, not extrapolated
One solve per step
Interpolation in condition space from labels; stall boundaries are not tracked


Mesh adaptation driven by error indicators
Resolution follows the solution’s own difficulty
Indicator evaluation and remeshing
Sampling density fixed by the dataset; the program’s density-robustness tests show large sensitivity in some configurations


Nondimensionalization and scaling
Inputs enter at unit scale by construction; conditioning is controlled
None
Left to the recipe; a dimensional freestream input produced a 2.8x artifact in this program (UDRV)


Conservation and compatibility enforced by construction
Fluxes balance across faces; Neumann data are compatible
Discretization design
Enforced only if the architecture is built for it; ISLA enforces symmetry contracts, not conservation

title: 6  What classical solvers do that surrogates do not
text:
6.2 Hypotheses this inventory generates
Each hypothesis names the ingredient it borrows, what would falsify it, and its relation to the program’s existing evidence. The order is by expected information per unit cost.

Global constraint by solve, local prediction by network (borrowed from projection methods). Predict the velocity or a surface quantity pointwise, then obtain pressure by solving the constraint it must satisfy (a Poisson solve for divergence-free velocity in the interior; for a surface-only task, a global consistency solve is not available, which is itself informative about why surface pressure is the hard target). Falsifier: on the DrivAerML volume task, pressure from a Poisson solve of the predicted velocity is no more accurate than the directly predicted pressure. Evidence bearing on it: ISLA’s interior velocity is the field it predicts best (0.64x GeoTransolver-volume); if the constraint solve turns that into a pressure advantage, the pointwise-pressure gap closes for a reason the mechanism names. Cost: one sparse solve per case at inference, no training change; can be run as an eval-only study on saved volume predictions if the sampled interior points support a discretization, otherwise on a coarse background grid with stated interpolation error.
Wall law as an architectural prior (borrowed from wall models). The program’s eddy-viscosity gap and the audit’s wall-flux spectrum argument both say the near-wall region needs resolution the interior does not. A surrogate that predicts wall shear through a learned local law of wall distance, local velocity and local pressure gradient, with the same law on every wall, would transfer that law across families. Falsifier: a local law fitted on DrivAerML does not reduce wall-shear error on the SHIFT-SUV fastback relative to a direct prediction. This is a component evaluation with target labels used only for scoring.
Near-field / far-field split with analytic translation (borrowed from fast multipole). The composition study (Chapter 4) tests whether local responses compose; the exterior variant asks whether far-field interactions between separated bodies can be analytic while only near-field maps are learned. Falsifier: on the five-sphere family, a truncated multipole coupling with exact local responses fails to reproduce the reference pressure difference the audit resolved (0.005 in pressure coefficient) at an order that stays fixed as bodies move apart.
Residual as a control signal (borrowed from iterative solvers). Even without a certificate, a residual of an available approximate operator (potential flow with a wake model, or a coarse RANS operator) evaluated on the surrogate’s prediction may rank cases by difficulty and flag failures. Falsifier: the residual’s correlation with the true per-case error is below 0.5 on held-out families, or no better than the model’s own seed disagreement (which the program measured at +0.67 in-family at 35 cases and near zero at 1,260). The value is triage, not accuracy.
Learned smoother or prolongation on a classical hierarchy (borrowed from multigrid, the surviving form of the audit’s fourth direction after Chapter 5). The coarse space stays geometric; the network learns the part classical methods choose heuristically (smoother weights, prolongation stencils) conditioned on local operator entries. Prerequisite gate: exhibit an operator class where the classical hierarchy degrades (anisotropy, high Péclet, a state-dependent Jacobian); without such a failure there is nothing to learn.
Continuation instead of extrapolation (borrowed from Newton and continuation methods). Regime extrapolation fails for every architecture tested; a solver would not extrapolate across stall but continue from the nearest solved angle. A surrogate conditioned on a nearby solution (the audit’s state-conditioned extension) rather than on the condition alone is the learned analogue. Falsifier: conditioning on the field at the nearest in-distribution angle does not reduce the post-stall error below the unconditioned surrogate’s. This needs volume or surface fields at the neighbouring condition at inference, which changes the product.
Conservation by construction. A surrogate whose surface pressure and shear integrate to forces that satisfy a momentum balance with a predicted wake deficit would carry a physical constraint no current model enforces. Falsifier: enforcing the balance as a hard or soft constraint does not reduce force error on held-out families. This is the weakest of the seven as a transfer mechanism, because the constraint is a single scalar relation per case.

title: 6  What classical solvers do that surrogates do not
text:
6.3 Priority and what runs first
Hypotheses 1 and 4 are eval-only on artifacts that exist and are queued behind the controls. Hypothesis 2 is a two-lane component evaluation and a natural companion to the program’s eddy-viscosity work. Hypothesis 3 rides on the composition study’s exterior variant. Hypotheses 5 through 7 are gated on prerequisites (a failing classical hierarchy; neighbouring-condition fields at inference; a conservation relation with predictive content) and are recorded here so that they are not rediscovered later without their falsifiers.

title: Lab notebook
text:
2026-09-09 — Program start: from the audit’s agenda to preregistered experiments
Setting. The companion review of the ISLA record (research/cross_dataset_generalization/, untracked; rendered report at its _book/index.html) audited the repository, thirty-one primary papers and five analytic controls, and concluded that the record does not establish a cross-dataset accuracy advantage for ISLA; with the freestream input matched, GeoTransolver and Transolver are more accurate at both completed HiLiftAeroML rungs, and on the DrivAerML → SHIFT-SUV fastback transfer ISLA’s source-only error is 0.99 against GeoTransolver’s 0.59, both falling to 0.11–0.13 when the estate family joins training. The review proposed four directions (rich computational support with independent queries; topology- and conditioning-aware boundary responses; local flux responses with numerical global coupling; transferred correction spaces), a physical-input prerequisite, and a nonlinear extension.
Decision. This program runs in a worktree parallel to the main ISLA session (which owns the program book and its cluster lanes) and keeps in sync with it at milestones. Order of work, as the review recommended: controls first (C1 pressure-offset versus spatial error, eval-only on saved predictions; C2 source-only normalization audit; C3 a paired physical-condition control with exact labels), then in parallel the computational-support study (D1, which needs training lanes and therefore node budget from the main program) and the three nonlearned gates (D2 boundary-response rank and basis transfer on 2D Laplace; D3 local-response composition on 2D diffusion ports; D4 solver correction-space transfer on 2D finite-element systems), each run by a separate agent in its own worktree with a preregistration written before its first run. A literature chapter (L) asks what classical solvers do that surrogates do not.
Heilmeier answers, compressed. We want field and force predictions on geometries and families outside the training distribution without a new labeled dataset. Today’s surrogates fit their family and fail outside it, and the largest reported advantages in this program turned out to be protocol artifacts. The new element is not an architecture but a set of gates: each proposed mechanism has a cheap nonlearned test that can reject it before training. If it works, the payoff is a surrogate whose failure modes are understood and whose accuracy is stated with its cost. The risks are that no mechanism passes its gate (a useful negative), or that a passing gate does not carry to turbulent 3D data. Cost: CPU studies today; one four-lane training study when budget allows.

title: Lab notebook
section: 2026-09-09 — Preregistered: C1, pressure-offset versus spatial error on the fastback transfer
text:
2026-09-09 — Preregistered: C1, pressure-offset versus spatial error on the fastback transfer
Setting. DrivAerML (static wheels, fixed freestream, OpenFOAM hybrid RANS–LES) and SHIFT-SUV (rolling floor, rotating wheels, a different freestream speed and a different detached-eddy formulation) are different label-generating conventions on smooth single-body car families. Pressure is nondimensionalized by each dataset’s own metadata (q_∞) and not shifted, so a difference in the two datasets’ pressure reference would appear in a zero-shot prediction as a per-case constant, and a constant is exactly what makes a relative L2 error approach 1.0 when the predicted field is otherwise sensible. ISLA’s source-only fastback error is 0.99; GeoTransolver’s 0.59.
Instrument (eval-only). From the saved zero-shot predictions (smoke_fastback/{mt2_v3c,gt_fixed,mt2_multi,gt_multi}_seed{42,43,44}, 99 fastback cases) and the in-family DrivAerML evaluations of the same checkpoints, with cell areas recomputed from the saved triangles and cell normals from the saved mesh: per case and arm (seed-mean predictions), the area-weighted mean error (the offset), the centered remainder, the share of area-weighted squared error carried by the offset, the relative L2 error of the full and of the offset-removed error against the centered true field, the surface closedness |Σ a n| / Σ a, and the relative error of the integrated pressure force with and without the offset. Script: studies/controls/pressure_offset_diagnostic.py.
Bars, in readout units. For the two source-only fastback arms: offset-dominated if the constant carries ≥ 50% of the area-weighted squared error (median over cases) and the offset-removed relative L2 is at most 0.6 of the full one; spatial if the constant carries ≤ 20%; between, mixed. The in-family arms must show an offset share ≤ 10%, or the instrument is not measuring a transfer effect. Force: on surfaces with closedness ≤ 0.05 the force error with and without the offset must agree within the offset’s share, or the normals are inconsistent and the force reading is withdrawn.
What each outcome changes. Offset-dominated: the historical transfer gap is a label-convention question before it is an architecture question; C3 (paired physical conditions) becomes the next control, and any transfer claim must state the pressure reference. Spatial: the gap is a genuine field error; the offset hypothesis is closed and D1/D2 proceed on their own merits. Either way the readout is descriptive: target labels are used only to diagnose, never to correct predictions.

section: 2026-09-09 — Verdict: C1 spatial — the zero-shot fastback error is a field error, not a pressure-reference offset (offset share 1.5–2.6% for ISLA, 3.0–3.2% for GeoTransolver)
text:
2026-09-09 — Verdict: C1 spatial — the zero-shot fastback error is a field error, not a pressure-reference offset (offset share 1.5–2.6% for ISLA, 3.0–3.2% for GeoTransolver)
Readout (2026-09-09 — Preregistered: C1, pressure-offset versus spatial error on the fastback transfer; studies/controls/pressure_offset_2026-09-09.json; 99 fastback cases, 48 DrivAerML validation cars; seed-mean predictions; the GeoTransolver source-only and in-family arms use seeds 45 and 46 because the seed 42–44 predictions of the historical reduction are no longer on disk, the configuration being identical). Verdict: spatial, for both architectures. The constant carries 1.5% (ISLA) and 3.0% (GeoTransolver) of the source-only squared error by the median over cases (2.6% and 3.2% by the mean), far below the 20% floor of the “spatial” band; removing it changes the relative error by under 1%. The in-family arms pass the instrument check (offset share under 1%). The offsets that do exist are small and of the same sign for both models (+0.14 of the true field’s RMS), which is consistent with a modest difference of pressure reference between the datasets but explains none of the gap. The transfer failure is a spatial field error, and it is also a force error: 1.6x (ISLA) and 1.4x (GeoTransolver) of the true force magnitude against 0.04 in-family, falling to 0.28 and 0.20 when the estate family joins training.
What it changes. The pressure-reference hypothesis is closed. The compound physical-condition mismatch between the datasets (ground and wheel motion, freestream speed, solver formulation) remains the leading explanation that is not about architecture, and C3 tests its logic on an exactly specified problem. Any transfer claim in this program states the force error alongside the field error, since a field error of 0.9 is a force error above 100%.

title: Lab notebook
section: 2026-09-09 — Verdict: D4 stops — a free geometric coarse grid beats a frozen source-fitted correction space on every held-out elliptic system
text:
2026-09-09 — Verdict: D4 stops — a free geometric coarse grid beats a frozen source-fitted correction space on every held-out elliptic system
The solver-space probe (studies/solver_spaces/, preregistered in its PREREG.md before the run, 47 s on one CPU) compared a frozen proper orthogonal decomposition of smoother-resistant source errors against equal-dimension classical coarse spaces on 2D finite-element diffusion systems with holes, under within-family, topology and coefficient shifts. The frozen space left 0.75–0.96 of the slow-mode error where the geometric coarse grid left 0.47–0.73 (ratios 0.62–0.76 against bars of 2.0 and 1.5), and complete solves with it cost 19–72% more work than with the classical space; the per-target oracle decomposition lost to the grid as well. The mechanism is that solution snapshots span the right-hand sides seen at the source geometries, not the operator’s slow subspace, which for an elliptic operator under a point smoother is generic smoothness and comes free. The convection–diffusion variant was uninformative at mesh Péclet 0.5 and is recorded as not measured. Chapter 5  Transferring a solver correction space has the tables; the direction’s only remaining homes are operator classes where classical coarse spaces fail, and learned smoothers or prolongations on a classical hierarchy, both behind prerequisite gates (6  What classical solvers do that surrogates do not).

title: Lab notebook
section: 2026-09-09 — C2, source-only normalization: audited from the configurations, one item flagged
text:
2026-09-09 — C2, source-only normalization: audited from the configurations, one item flagged
Both transfer dataset configurations (drivaer_ml_surface.yaml, shift_suv_fastback_surface.yaml) nondimensionalize pressure and wall shear by each case’s own metadata (dynamic pressure) with no shift, and normalize wall shear by a declared per-dataset constant (standard deviation 0.00313 for DrivAerML, 0.00183 for SHIFT-SUV; zero mean). Inference denormalizes predictions with the statistics saved at training time (source-side), and the relative L2 metric is invariant to a common scale, so the differing wall shear constants do not bias the reported relative errors; they would bias any absolute or mixed-field loss. Pressure carries no normalization constant beyond the physical nondimensionalization, so the C1 result is not a normalization artifact either. Flagged: the wall-shear constant is target-side in the target configuration (a statistic of SHIFT-SUV chosen when its config was written); for a zero-shot protocol the target configuration should carry the source’s constant, which changes nothing for relative metrics and is recorded here as a protocol rule. Verdict: normalizations are source-only in effect for the reported metrics; one declared-constant hygiene item.

title: Lab notebook
section: 2026-09-09 — Verdict: D3 not worth a learner as proposed — smooth-mode local errors are amplified 4–30x by the interface solve and grids grow superlinearly; the surviving form is a hybrid with exact low modes
text:
2026-09-09 — Verdict: D3 not worth a learner as proposed — smooth-mode local errors are amplified 4–30x by the interface solve and grids grow superlinearly; the surviving form is a hybrid with exact low modes
The composition gate (studies/composition/, preregistered in its PREREG.md, 1,064 s on one CPU) assembled 2D finite-element diffusion components with identical straight ports into chains and grids of 2–16 components and perturbed every local response by a relative Frobenius error ε. Exact composition is exact (composition law 2 × 10⁻¹⁶, interface solve 5 × 10⁻¹⁵). At ε = 10⁻² the median global energy error is 1.7% for two components, 7% for chains of eight, 33% for grids of eight and 34% for grids of sixteen (a 6.2x growth from four to sixteen, faster than linear), missing the 5% bar; errors concentrated on rough port modes are damped 20–100x while errors on smooth modes are amplified 4–30x and set the global error, since the smooth small-eigenvalue part of a response carries the load (truncating a response below 63 of 64 modes fails catastrophically). Transfer-optimal port modes transfer to new shapes but need 13–15 of 15 modes for 1%; proper-orthogonal modes are shape-specific; at rank 4 both leave 16–27% error, missing the reduction bar. The interface solve is cheaper than the monolithic solve only up to four components, and a partition-of-unity coarse space does not help the iteration count. The narrow-channel family did not place a barrier at a port, so the near-field claim is untested by this instrument. Verdict against the bars: not worth a learner as proposed. What survives is a hybrid solver (exact smooth low-mode response, learned rough remainder), with a split-response test and a port-adjacent barrier family as its next nonlearned gates, not launched here. Chapter 4  Local-response composition has the tables; figures studies/composition/fig_*.png.

title: Lab notebook
section: 2026-09-09 — D1 launched: six lanes for computational support with a depth-matched passive readout
text:
2026-09-09 — D1 launched: six lanes for computational support with a depth-matched passive readout
What was built (merged from the D1 track, commit 834bd779e on this branch). ISLA(support_tokens=True, query_independent=True, n_query_scalars=1, query_mass="source_total", n_decoder_layers=K): the forward takes support_points / support_normals / support_scalars, which join the encoder as interacting tokens with the same invariant seeds, a token-type offset and a learned total mass equal to a learned fraction of the total source measure; requested query_points / query_normals / query_scalars are decoded passively through K read blocks that see the final slice states, the anchors and a normalized log-space kernel readout of all encoder tokens. Ten contract tests pass (exact query independence with the support fixed, at 1e-12, alone or with 500 foreign companions; SE(3) covariance; drive degree one; measure-scale and source-refinement invariance; gauge scale equivariance; geo_checkpoint exactness; every parameter receives gradients); the existing ISLA suites (63) pass. Recipe: a SplitInteriorSupport transform moves the first n_support interior points of the reader’s deterministic per-case sample into a boundaries.support mesh carrying the signed distance and its gradient; dataset drivaer_ml_volume_support.yaml (10,000 vehicle cells by boundary_subsample: cells, 10,000 interior points split 5,000 support + 5,000 queries); model isla_volume_support.yaml.
Lanes (jobs 691276–691281, names v0sup-0..5, launcher v0/v0_support_aga.sbatch, code snapshot code_support, recipe copy recipe_support so the program’s frozen recipe is untouched; frozen V0 protocol, unit-direction drive, 500 epochs, lr 1e-3, bf16, seeds 42/43): SUPPORT-12 (v0_isla_support12_seed{42,43}), PASSIVE-12 (v0_isla_passive12_seed{42,43}: no support tokens, 12 read blocks with the SDF scalar) and SUPPORT-4 (v0_isla_support4_seed{42,43}). Node budget confirmed by the main session (25 → 31 of 32 program nodes). Two cluster conventions were reconciled before submission and are recorded here: the frozen recipe’s model configs carry # @package _global_ (added to the repository yaml too) and address surface tokens as boundaries.vehicle.cell_normals / cell_areas, so the cluster copy of the model yaml uses those keys while the repository yaml keeps the nested cell_data.* keys of the upstream-merged recipe; model overrides are model.<kwarg>.
References and bars (PREREG.md, written before launch). The support arms read 10,000 vehicle cells, so their primary reference is the QT+SDF arm at 10,000 cells (0.0572 / 0.0848 / 0.1187), with the ~365-cell arm (0.0567 / 0.0853 / 0.1215) reported alongside since V0-SURF10K showed the two differ by under 3%. Supported if SUPPORT-12 is within 3% of the reference on all three fields (≤ 0.0584 / 0.0879 / 0.1251 against the 365-cell numbers as preregistered; ≤ 0.0589 / 0.0873 / 0.1223 against the 10k-cell numbers, both reported) and the sentinel error is independent of the companion count within the bf16 floor measured on the legacy passive checkpoint; falsified if pressure ≥ 0.0624; between, the SUPPORT-4 and PASSIVE-12 arms decompose depth against interaction.

title: Lab notebook
section: 2026-09-09 — Finding while building D1: the legacy passive kernel readout clamps the kernel mass, so far-from-surface queries scale with the absolute source weights
text:
2026-09-09 — Finding while building D1: the legacy passive kernel readout clamps the kernel mass, so far-from-surface queries scale with the absolute source weights
In physicsnemo/experimental/nn/isla/model.py, the passive decoder’s local token readout _kernel_readout(q_r, src_r, src_h, src_w, rho, eps) (called from _ReadBlock.forward when src_h is given, with rho = local_readout_rho, default 0.02 in gauge-normalized coordinates) computes k = exp(-d²/ρ²) · w and divides by mass = k.sum(-1).clamp_min(eps). For a query farther than a few ρ from every source point the true mass is below eps = 1e-12, the clamp replaces it, and the readout becomes Σ k h / eps, which scales with the absolute source weights instead of being a weighted mean: in the D1 track’s test a 4.2x rescale of the source weights moved the legacy passive output by 0.16 in relative norm at such queries. With ρ = 0.02 and interior queries whose median wall distance is about 5 mm on a 4 m car (below ρ in gauge units) most queries are inside the kernel’s reach, but the far tail of the interior sample is not, so the legacy passive arm’s 2.6x pressure deficit (program book, interior chapter) includes a contribution from this readout regime that the arm’s measure-scale contract test did not exercise. The legacy path is left bitwise unchanged so trained checkpoints reproduce; the support path uses an exactly normalized log-space form (softmax over sources with logits −d²/ρ² + log w), identical where the mass is not tiny. The PASSIVE-12 arm, which uses the normalized readout with 12 read blocks and the SDF scalar, bounds how much of the 2.6x was readout and depth rather than passivity; the main session has asked for this note to attach a caveat to that figure once the arm reports.
